# Arpente

> Arpente is a free journal of walks and hikes for iPhone, in French and English. It records each exploration with GPS, draws it on a map, and keeps its distance, duration, elevation gain, notes and photos. It isn't a performance app: no rankings, no feed, no followers. No account, no ads: your routes are stored on your iPhone and in your private iCloud. Made by Wibeset in Canada.

Key facts:

- Platform: iPhone only (not available on Android or the web). Coming soon to the App Store.
- Price: free, with no ads, no subscription and no account.
- Idea: a journal of explorations rather than a fitness tracker. A 2 km walk around the block and an 18 km hike in the mountains are both worth keeping.
- Privacy: routes, locations, notes and photos are stored on the device and synced with the user's private iCloud; the developer never receives them. Location is used only while recording.
- Maps: Apple Maps.
- Statistics: distance, duration and elevation gain, by month and by year, plus a map of every place explored.
- Export: each route as a GPX file.

- [Home](https://arpente.app/)
- [Support](https://arpente.app/support/)
- [Privacy](https://arpente.app/privacy/)
- [Strava alternative](https://arpente.app/strava-alternative/): Looking for a Strava alternative for walks and hikes? Arpente is a free iPhone journal with GPS maps and no account, no feed, no followers and no leaderboards.
- [AllTrails alternative](https://arpente.app/alltrails-alternative/): Looking for a free AllTrails alternative to record your hikes? Arpente is an iPhone hiking journal with GPS maps, elevation and GPX export. No account, no subscription.
- [Komoot alternative](https://arpente.app/komoot-alternative/): Looking for a simple Komoot alternative? Arpente is a free iPhone journal of your walks and hikes: GPS maps, statistics and GPX export, with no account and no paid regions.
- [Walking journal](https://arpente.app/walking-journal/): Arpente is a walking and hiking journal app for iPhone: each walk with its GPS map, distance, time, elevation, a note and photos. Free, no account, no ads.
- [Private hiking tracker](https://arpente.app/private-hiking-tracker/): A private hiking and walking tracker for iPhone: no account, no public profile, no feed. Arpente keeps your GPS routes on your iPhone and in your private iCloud.
- [GPX export](https://arpente.app/gpx-export/): How to record a walk or hike on iPhone and export it as a GPX file with Arpente, then open it in another mapping or hiking app. Free, no account.
- [Free walking app](https://arpente.app/free-walking-app/): Arpente is a free walking app for iPhone: record your walks with GPS, see your distance, time and elevation, and keep a journal. No ads, no subscription, no account.
- [Hikes in Québec](https://arpente.app/quebec-hikes/): Mont Albert in Gaspésie, the Acropole des Draveurs in Charlevoix and the Sentier de la Statue on the Saguenay Fjord: distance, elevation and tips for three great Québec hikes.
- [Walks in Montréal](https://arpente.app/montreal-walks/): The Lachine Canal path, Mount Royal up to the Kondiaronk lookout, and a loop through your own neighbourhood: three walks in Montréal to record and keep.
- [Mont Albert](https://arpente.app/quebec-hikes/mont-albert/): Hiking Mont Albert in Parc national de la Gaspésie: 11.6 km return by the north side or a 17.3 km loop, about 860 m of climbing. Map, elevation profile, photos and tips.
- [Acropole des Draveurs](https://arpente.app/quebec-hikes/acropole-des-draveurs/): Hiking the Acropole des Draveurs in Parc national des Hautes-Gorges-de-la-Rivière-Malbaie: about 10.4 km return and 800 m of climbing. Map, elevation profile, photos and tips.
- [Sentier de la Statue](https://arpente.app/quebec-hikes/sentier-de-la-statue/): Hiking the Sentier de la Statue from Baie-Éternité to Notre-Dame-du-Saguenay, above the Saguenay Fjord: about 7.6 km return. Map, elevation profile, photos and tips.
- [Lachine Canal](https://arpente.app/montreal-walks/lachine-canal/): Walking the Lachine Canal path in Montréal, from the Old Port to Lachine: 14.5 km, flat, past locks, old factories and the Atwater Market. Map, photos and tips.
- [Mount Royal](https://arpente.app/montreal-walks/mount-royal/): Walking up Mount Royal in Montréal from the top of rue Peel to the Kondiaronk lookout and the cross: about 2 km one way and 150 m of climbing. Map, profile, photos and tips.
